direction: Narrow the benchmark claim to what is unmatched: version-level gold labels (which clause version is authoritative) plus recency-decoupled strata and an answer-differential screen, delivered on amended regulatory text. Do not claim novelty for 'a temporal legal benchmark' or for corpus construction, since legal MCQA with temporal validity, point-in-time financial QA and ESG temporal benchmarks already exist. State explicitly that no directly matching benchmark was found in the searched literature within a budget-limited search, and plan a re-check of the closest legal resource (LEGAL-LINK-EU) to see whether its data can be extended to version-level retrieval, in which case the contribution rests on the measurement and the cross-retriever test rather than on the resource.
hypothesis: A benchmark whose gold labels identify the clause version in force at a time-stamped query, with recency-decoupled strata, exposes version-selection failures that existing temporal legal MCQA and point-in-time financial benchmarks do not measure, and it shows whether valid-time gating or recency decay is required.
rationale: The comparison shows the benchmark space is crowded at the level of 'temporal legal or regulatory QA' but empty at the level of version-level retrieval labels with recency-decoupled strata, and the legal-retrieval review independently identifies document-granularity versioning as an unaddressed failure mode. Narrowing the claim to that specific measurement keeps a defensible contribution while dropping claims that the comparison contradicts. It deserves investigation next because the resource is the load-bearing element of the remaining contribution, and its novelty depends on precisely this distinction rather than on corpus rarity.
research_question: Does a version-level, recency-decoupled retrieval benchmark over amended regulatory text reveal version-selection failures that established temporal legal MCQA and point-in-time financial benchmarks do not capture, and does it show that valid-time gating is required where recency decay is not sufficient?
